title: Pontificale simply calls them ‘Churches’ dedicated in Saints’ honor and name—without Bellarmino’s temple/basilica split
source_text: XVII. Caeterum Pontificale Romanum de aedium sacrarum dedicatione sive consecratione agens, nec templi, nec basilicae nomine eas designat, sed simpliciter Ecclesias vocat, ac sub ea appellatione dicit eas in honore & nomine Sanctorum dedicari. Nam pag. 173. editionis Parisiensis anni 1615. Jubet ut in litaniis quae in ejusmodi solemni dedicatione recitari solent, suo loco ibi nominetur Sanctus ille in cujus honore & nomine Ecclesia dedicatur. Et postea Pontifex saepius Deum rogat ut Ecclesiam quam consecrat, velit in memoriam hujus vel illius Sancti purificare; & benedicere.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover the Roman Pontifical, treating of the dedication or consecration of sacred houses, designates them neither by the name of temple nor of basilica, but simply calls them Churches, and under that appellation says they are dedicated in the honor and name of the Saints. For on page 173 of the Paris edition of the year 1615 it orders that in the litanies which are customarily recited in such a solemn dedication, that Saint be named in his place in whose honor and name the Church is dedicated. And afterward the Pontiff often asks God that He will to purify and bless the Church which he consecrates in memory of this or that Saint.
pass_b_english: The Pontificale skips temple/basilica jargon and simply consecrates ‘Churches’ in Saints’ honor and name.
Litanies name the title Saint; the bishop asks God to purify the church in that Saint’s memory.

lemmas.gloss: in the honor and name of the Saints
